hypotheses.claim: The is_select effect in attribute_effect unconditionally calls select_option(select, prev.value) with undefined when the spread has no value prop; since it runs after mounting, select_option's non-mounting branch sets selectedIndex = -1, wiping the browser's default 'selected' option.
evidence_refs: attributes.js:517-523 (is_select effect always calls select_option(select, prev.value), even when spread has no 'value' key)
select.js:30-44 (select_option: no option matches undefined and mounting is undefined, so selectedIndex = -1)
hypotheses.prediction: Guarding the select_option call so it only runs when a 'value' key exists in prev will make selects[1].value === 'o2' in both dom and hydrate modes of the holdout test.
hypotheses.falsifier: If after guarding, selects[1].value is still '' (e.g., the reset happens elsewhere such as set_attributes or template claiming), the hypothesis is wrong.

hypotheses.claim: The reset comes from set_attributes or hydration/template claim logic mutating the select's options or attributes, not from select_option.
hypotheses.prediction: No code path in set_attributes touches select.value or option.selected for a spread containing only onclick, so a guard in attribute_effect alone will fix the test.
hypotheses.falsifier: If a trace in set_attributes shows selectedIndex being reset there, this hypothesis is right and the select_option guard will not fix the test.
